a.summary: Only one of the two public array-taking createTx overloads got the new in-place-mutation javadoc; the AddressLookupTable overload compacts the caller's array identically and is still undocumented — and it is the code path the documented overload's own one-table promise is delegated to.
a.failure_scenario: A consumer holds its own sorted AccountMeta[] and calls Transaction.createTx(instructions, serializedInstructionLength, sorted, lookupTable) (the AddressLookupTable overload at line 266). Lines 273-320 permute `sorted` in place exactly as the documented overload does — message accounts to the front, lookup accounts to the tail. The caller then reuses `sorted` (for a second transaction, or to map account index -> meta) and gets the permuted array: with input [payer, lookupA, lookupB, program] the array is [payer, program, lookupA, lookupB] on return, so index-based lookups and any second createTx call read the wrong accounts. Nothing at the declaration warns them. The same consumer reading the newly documented 4-arg overload is told 'With one or more lookup tables, compacts sortedAccounts in place' — but the one-table case is delivered by line 447 delegating to this undocumented sibling, so the documented sentence is realized by a method whose own signature carries no such notice.

b.summary: The javadoc documents the in-place caller-array mutation on only one of the two public createTx overloads that perform it; the sibling AddressLookupTable overload runs the identical compaction and stays silent, and the documented overload delegates to it.
b.failure_scenario: A consumer builds `sorted = TransactionRecord.sortV0Accounts(map)` and calls `Transaction.createTx(ixs, len, sorted, table)` (the single-AddressLookupTable overload). Lines 298-306 compact `sorted` in place, so it returns partitioned as {message accounts..., lookup accounts...} and is no longer in VO_META_COMPARATOR order. The consumer, having read no warning on that overload, reuses `sorted` for a second call with a different lookup table that does not carry those accounts. The previously-skipped writable accounts are now included, producing a wire account list ordered payer(write,signer), program(readonly), lookupA(write), lookupB(write) with numReadonlyUnsignedAccounts=1 - so the runtime reads the last non-signer as the readonly one and grants the program account write privilege while stripping it from a writable account.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
